purpose: Output-level voice contract for the sky placement (planet-in-sign) articles on /#sky/placement. Implements apps/web/src/content/sky-writing/TLDR-Sky-Article-Spec.md as machine-usable rules. Applies to RENDERED article copy in the three slots (hook / lived / turn), not to source meaning in data/. Enforced by scripts/lint-placement-voice.js; taste enforced by scripts/judge-placement-voice.js.
voiceDescription: Direct, modern, and emotionally exact. The article is not a sign encyclopedia; its job is to give the reader one memorable way to recognize the transit in real life. Interesting before comprehensive. Verbs and scenes over adjective triplets. Prefer a clear observation over a polished abstraction. A memorable phrase earns its place only when it makes literal sense on the first read.
personNote: Current Sky describes shared weather. Sky-to-sky placement copy uses collective language: 'we', 'someone', a named group, or a concrete shared scene. Do not use the generic noun 'people'; name the actual subject. Never use 'you', 'your', 'yours', 'yourself', or 'yourselves'. Second person belongs to transit-to-natal copy. Historical owner-approved originals are preserved verbatim for provenance even when they predate current surface rules; they are not permission for newly generated copy to repeat retired language.

exemplarStatePolicy.historical_owner_approved: Original owner-approved copy preserved verbatim for provenance. Never supplied to the active Current Sky judge as positive evidence.
exemplarStatePolicy.collective_adaptation_candidate: A collective-language editorial adaptation. It may be a controlled rule-compliance test input, but remains needs_review, ownerApproved false, and promotionAuthorized false.
exemplarStatePolicy.current_sky_owner_approved: A collective version explicitly approved by the owner. Only this state is eligible for active positive judge-calibration evidence. Calibration eligibility does not make an article canonical production copy, authorize governed content promotion, or authorize generation evidence.

punctuation.emDash: The em dash is banned. Use a spaced hyphen ' - ' or restructure.
punctuation.example: Build from the inside out and people notice.

articleStructure.note: Owner-provided structural models (2026-07-27): CHANI's 'Horoscopes for the Sun in Leo' and 'Your guide to Jupiter in Leo'. STRUCTURE is borrowed, never their copy. The page renders top to bottom as: (1) TAGLINE - one clear full sentence under the title; (2) WHEN - the computed date range from ephemeris, never generated; (3) PRIOR-SIGN HANDOFF when engine facts exist; (4) QUOTE - the first sentence of the hook, promoted by the reader into its own bold callout and removed from the body; (5) MEANING, including the CYCLE LINE when reviewed cycle facts exist; (6) LIVED - the body with pace and useful expression; (7) TURN - the observable distortion or confrontation; (8) CONCURRENT EVENTS when ranked engine events exist; (9) MOVES - 2-3 concrete ways to work with the transit, each one specific sentence; (10) COMPUTED EVENTS - dated aspects/lunations during the transit render from ephemeris. CHANI's cultural 'last time this happened' history section is EXCLUDED: only an engine-supplied prior residency date range may appear, because cultural or historical characterization would require sources we do not have.

factGatedSlots.rule: At or immediately before the hook, use one sentence saying where the planet arrives from and what changes. Use the supplied {{priorSign}}, {{priorSignEntryDate}}, and {{priorSignExitDate}} resolver tokens instead of literal moving facts. Use collective language and the planet's name; never use an appositive planet definition.
factGatedSlots.houseExample: After a year of growing through what feels like home, Jupiter leaves Cancer and starts growing through the other person.

factGatedSlots.rule: The engine renders one reviewed cycle fact line directly under the computed date range. Every number must come from planet-cycle-facts.json. Write 'all twelve signs'; the word 'zodiac' is banned. Do not render this slot for the Moon. The writer must not repeat the cycle line in article prose; duration belongs in prose only when it carries additional meaning.
factGatedSlots.houseExample: Jupiter takes about twelve years to visit all twelve signs, so each sign gets roughly one year of this attention.

factGatedSlots.rule: Between the turn and moves, use one short paragraph explaining how the top one or two engine-ranked events inside the transit window change how the placement lands. Dates come from the engine and meaning comes from the astrology library. If no ranked events exist, omit the slot.
factGatedSlots.houseExample: A month into the transit, the South Node follows into the same sign, and the year of expansion picks up an undertow: what grows here also gets tested here.

articleStructure.taglineRules: One clear full sentence readers understand on first read, normally 6-18 words. Strong is welcome; cryptic compression is not. Use plain everyday words.
articleStructure.movesRules: 2-3 items. Each is one sentence, a specific doable action tied to THIS placement (CHANI model: 'emcee an open mic', not 'embrace the energy'). No generic coaching verbs (embrace, trust, align, manifest). A move that would work for any placement fails the swap test.

timingDevices.rule: Timing devices are fact-gated and render at most once. Date ranges may come only from the engine. They do not authorize cultural or historical claims. A qualitative, non-numeric subperiod such as 'a few months in,' 'early in the transit,' or 'by midyear' may trace to a reviewed residency fact only when it cannot exceed that residency. Numeric or date-like subperiods such as 'four months in,' 'in March,' or 'by the 15th' require an explicit engine fact or render token.

devices.rule: The article may state the previous residency's date range when the engine supplies both boundaries. Use {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} and {{previousResidencyExitDate}} instead of literal dates. State the dates only; never add celebrity, pop-culture, political, or era characterization.
devices.houseExample: Jupiter was last in Leo from July 2014 to August 2015.

formatExemplarPolicy.requiredAuthority: exact owner approval for generation evidence
formatExemplarPolicy.approvalScope: voice-format evidence only; not factual approval, production approval, canonical copy, or serving promotion
formatExemplarPolicy.rule: Supply only exact owner-approved cards listed in eligible. Their five slots guide register and beat movement; they are not the continuous fallback structure.

voiceDevices.rule: Permissions, not requirements. Use zero, one, or two only when the device fits the placement and keeps natural English.

devices.rule: The opening may show the meeting of two archetypes in one balanced sentence.
devices.example: The sign that multiplies meets the planet that refines. Gemini speaks in options; Saturn speaks in absolutes.

devices.rule: The turn may use two or three parallel 'the way X becomes Y' clauses, never more.
devices.example: The way perfectionism becomes protection against criticism, the way busy-ness becomes a hedge against feeling, the way fixing others becomes an escape from our own healing.

devices.rule: The lived section or turn may close on one pair of parallel questions.
devices.example: Where have we exhausted ourselves defending something no longer worth the fight? Where have we built walls that now trap us rather than protect us?

devices.rule: The article may coin a short, plain-words name for the psychological pattern it describes.

memeScenePolicy.rule: A scene that any astrology account would attach to this sign fails. Derive the scene from this placement's combined meaning at this transit's scale. Apply this check to the central opening, tension, and development sequence. Isolated practical moves are exempt unless the central scene itself is the prohibited scene.
memeScenePolicy.scaleRule: A year-long or slower transit cannot be illustrated only by one evening's logistics.

libra: invitation scheduling used as the transit's central stakes

items: We can choose one long-term goal and give it a weekly appointment with a defined stopping point.
We can write down one responsibility carried alone, then ask a specific person to take a defined part of it.
We can leave work at the promised time once this week, even with more still left to do.
movesExemplar.rule: Use this exact list as a register and movement exemplar for practical actions. Do not treat it as production copy for another placement.

shape.note: The three authored beats at the article's core, rendered into three content slots. An authored planet-sign trio always wins over the per-planet fallback. Optional current-aspect line is COMPUTED at runtime and appended below the article; it is never generated here and never carries invented dates.

beats.does: 2-4 sentences. Sentence 1 is the standalone recognition quote: a complete line someone would remember or send to a friend. The reader promotes it into a bold callout and removes it from the article body. Begin with a lived premise, not a slogan or abstract placement summary. The remaining sentences form the meaning paragraph: explain what the planet governs and how the sign changes its method, pace, or priorities. Translate meaning into natural prose and behavior, never a keyword list. Name the transit only after the human situation is clear when possible.
beats.example: A familiar role starts to feel too small. The Sun describes identity, vitality, and the need to be fully seen; in Leo, that attention becomes warmer, more expressive, and harder to keep in the background.

beats.does: What the planet-sign combination does in ordinary life. 2-4 sentences. The engine renders the cycle facts outside the prose; mention duration here only when it adds meaning. Concrete evidence must be invented fresh for this placement. Keep the transit as the subject and use lived moments as evidence. Do not let one invented scenario carry the whole card, and do not line up examples as a coverage checklist. (The spec's classic illustrations - unsent message, corrected coffee order, overfilled calendar - are teaching examples and BANNED in output.) Explain the planet through behavior, never through a keyword list.
beats.example: Feelings get translated into tasks: make the list, keep the promise, handle the thing before it becomes a problem.

beats.does: Name where the gift becomes the problem and end with a clean truth. 2-5 sentences. The shadow must be observable behavior, not an abstract warning. Name the exact cost: the delayed conversation, cancelled plan, overspending, overwork, one-sided agreement, or other source-supported consequence. A directive is allowed when it is specific. End on the strongest plain sentence; no dramatic metaphor, second aphorism, blessing, or soft summary after it.
beats.example: Trying to be needed instead of loved can leave both needs unmet.

extendedSlots.does: One clear full sentence rendered under the article title, normally 6-18 words. It must make sense on first read rather than compressing the article into a cryptic slogan.
shapeExamples: The disagreement starts before the cancellation.
extendedSlots.shapeExamplesNote: Shape illustrations only, NOT owner-approved copy. Do not ship without review.

extendedSlots.does: 2-3 concrete ways to work with the transit, one sentence each, rendered as a short list after the turn. Each move must be specific enough to fail on the wrong placement.
shapeExamples: Put one unfinished thing you are proud of where somebody can see it this week.
Give credit out loud to the person who has been waiting for it.
extendedSlots.shapeExamplesNote: Shape illustrations only, NOT owner-approved copy. Do not ship without review.

pace.note: Approximate sign-transit duration per planet. The engine renders the reviewed cycle fact line under the date range. Article prose mentions duration only when it carries additional meaning; the writer is not required to repeat pace.

labels.moon: about two and a half days
labels.saturn: about two and a half years
labels.chiron: years in a sign, four to nine depending on the stretch

planetTierRegister.note: Register scales with planet speed. Fast placements read like a passing mood; slow ones read like an era. A generational placement is legitimately more sweeping; a Moon placement that sounds like an era is overreach.

hints.luminary: felt, immediate, day-to-month scale; concrete micro-moments
hints.personal: the mind, worth, and drive over weeks; still concrete and personal
hints.social: commitments, structures, and story arcs over a year or two; may address groups and institutions
hints.generational: a shared era; a whole generation carries it together. World-scale claims are allowed; daily micro-moments still ground it.

loreBoundary: Sign lore, rulership, modality, elements-as-labels, symbols, and season history belong in an optional 'About [Sign]' block rendered separately, NEVER in the article body. The element may be felt in imagery (heat for Leo, depth for Scorpio) but never named as mechanics.

excludedStructures.natalFacing: Jupiter returns, natal houses, birth-chart personalization, and other transit-to-natal material do not belong in Current Sky placement copy. At most, include a one-line pointer to the app feature when the product supplies it.

culturalHistory.rule: Previous-residency copy may state an engine-supplied date range only. Celebrity references, pop-culture examples, political examples, and claims about what an era was like are excluded.
culturalHistory.mechanicalCoverage: The linter uses case-insensitive regex for the exact registered names above only; it does not infer shortened names, surnames, mononyms, stage names, or nicknames.
culturalHistory.judgeCoverage: Terra judges celebrity references not covered by the registered-name regex, including recognizable short forms, surnames, mononyms, stage names, and nicknames.

firstReadNaturalEnglish.rule: If a central sentence does not make literal sense in natural English, the article cannot receive a score of 2 or 3 unless the failure is isolated and the remaining article is strongly grounded.
scoreOneWhen: the hook contains opaque or unnatural personification
the lived section remains generalized, abstract, or lacks a recognizable sequence
mechanicalFailPatterns: \bthe banished want refuses to stay reasonable\b
examples: The banished want refuses to stay reasonable.
The first idea has spent its excitement.
The arrangement stopped telling the truth.

allowedCollectiveLanguage.rule: Do not flag someone or we merely because they are collective language. Current Sky does not use the generic noun people; name the group, person, message, decision, or behavior.

stackedEnding.rule: When the turn has already named the behavior and cost, any following slogan, metaphor, reassurance, or second conclusion should be marked for deletion.
stackedEnding.usualEffect: This usually lowers an otherwise strong article from 3 to 2. It does not require a full rewrite.

scoreThreeTolerance.rule: Score 3 does not require flawless prose. A minor explanatory or slightly broad sentence is acceptable when the placement remains unmistakable, the lived section is concrete, the turn names a real behavior and consequence, every hard surface rule passes, and no central sentence fails natural English.

judgeScoredChecks.name: read-aloud rule
judgeScoredChecks.rule: Read every sentence aloud. Score down wording that sounds compressed, overly composed, or unnatural when spoken.

judgeScoredChecks.name: morning-reader test
judgeScoredChecks.rule: Assume the reader has just woken up. Early sentences should be short, each opening sentence should carry one idea, and nothing should require a second read to parse.

humanJudgment: The seven calibration placements must remain distinct when read without their headings. If two could swap bodies without sounding wrong, the writing is not specific enough. This is the judge's swap test.
No compulsory coverage checklist: if a sentence exists only to satisfy coverage, cut it.

The transit is the subject: lived moments prove the placement, but one invented scenario must not carry the whole card. Related moments may reveal the same pressure without becoming a representative coverage list.
Do not flag 'someone' or 'we' merely because they are collective language. Current Sky does not use the generic noun 'people'. Name the group, message, decision, or behavior instead.

Everyday-language register: ordinary scenes use ordinary words. A dinner plan is not a counteroffer, both sides, meaningful influence, or a thoughtful compromise. Name what someone says, chooses, changes, refuses, or goes along with. Do not use 'tilt' as a dressed-up substitute for a change that can be stated directly.

Use ordinary current wording for communication. Default to message or response; reply and what they were told are also natural. Name an email, screenshot, notice, or physical letter only when the delivery method matters. Do not replace letter with portal notification, electronic correspondence, or automated communication.

First-read natural-English rule: read every sentence literally. An abstract noun may not perform an unnatural human action, and a metaphor may not require decoding. Conventional astrology language such as 'Mars governs action' is allowed. A central opaque sentence plus a generalized lived section is score 1; an isolated failure surrounded by strongly grounded writing may reach score 2, never 3.
Observation before polish: hooks begin with recognizable pressure, behavior, or a decision before explaining the placement. A slogan that merely sounds sharp is not a lived premise.

Turns name the actual cost and stop there. Once the behavior and cost have landed, mark any following slogan, metaphor, reassurance, second conclusion, or task-management assignment for deletion. The ending should leave the reader inside the consequence.
Reject coaching scaffolds such as 'the practical choice is,' 'the correction is not,' and 'the next choice is whether.' The development must state the transit, behavior, and consequence directly.

Cycle facts belong to the engine-rendered fact line directly under the date range. Do not reward writer prose for repeating the circuit or sign-stay numbers. Duration may appear in prose only when it carries additional meaning.

Do not infer employment or career from a sign alone. Taurus concerns money, resources, possessions, food, housing, the body, physical comfort, values, and self-worth; work language requires support from the planet, house, aspect, or supplied source.
Preserve strong owner-written lines. Do not replace a clear sentence merely to make it sound more polished.
One close with bite. A directive is allowed when specific; motivational recap never.
Vague 'things' as filler is off; idiomatic use ('handle the thing', 'get things done') is fine.
'heal' language is earned only where the placement is literally about a wound (Chiron); elsewhere it is coaching register. Judge concern, not regex.

A labeled 'The gift is X; the shadow is Y' seam reads as template and should be woven into behavior instead. A single 'The shadow is...' opener on a generational turn is allowed (see the Pluto exemplar). Judge concern, not regex.

ownerReviewedBeatCandidates.text: Uranus spends roughly seven years in a sign, long enough to pry open the quiet rules nobody admits are rules. The baseline shifts without warning: the person who held everything together stops answering every call, a guest room turns into an office, and an emergency contact list gets quietly rewritten. What looked like connection turns out to be heavy obligation, and home changes shape the moment the old structure demands more than anyone should give.
ownerReviewedBeatCandidates.use: Directional voice feedback for the lived beat: duration, baseline rupture, concrete changes, relational reclassification, cost. Specific physical changes beat broad metaphor; stay with the disruption instead of rushing into rebuilding. Do not treat the wording as owner-approved gold and do not copy it into another placement.

ownerApprovedCalibrationExamples.hook: The person who remembers every birthday, keeps the spare key, and gets called when someone needs help may stop doing all of it. Uranus in Cancer changes the private rules around home and family, especially the ones that only worked because one person was always available.
ownerApprovedCalibrationExamples.lived: Uranus spends roughly seven years in a sign, long enough to pry open the quiet rules nobody admits are rules. A sibling stops hosting every holiday, a guest room turns into an office, and the emergency contact list gets rewritten because the person everyone relied on is no longer willing to be the only plan. What looked like connection turns out to be heavy obligation, and home changes shape the moment the old arrangement demands more than anyone should give.
ownerApprovedCalibrationExamples.turn: Everyone may agree that the old setup was unfair and still expect the same person to fix it. They make the schedule, explain the new boundary, remind everyone what changed, and take the complaints when someone else is inconvenienced. A family role has not changed if one person is still doing all the work required to change it.
moves: Give one recurring responsibility to someone who will handle it without being reminded.
Update the emergency plan before the next emergency sends everyone back to the same person.
Change one room, routine, or family agreement that only works because one person keeps giving more than everyone else.
ownerApprovedCalibrationExamples.approvalScope: Exact v3 article wording only; judge-calibration evidence, not generation evidence, canonical production copy, or governed content promotion authorization.

exemplars.hook: Nobody claps for the thing we never show them. The Sun's move into Leo turns the lights on: a month of wanting to be seen doing it, not just having done it.
hookVariants: We can get good at staying in the background of our own lives. The Sun's month in Leo argues with that.
There is a difference between being humble and hiding. The Sun in Leo spends a month pressing on it.
exemplars.hookNote: Collective adaptation candidate derived from the owner-approved historical version. The adapted wording is not owner-approved and is not eligible as active Current Sky gold evidence.
exemplars.lived: For about a month, warmth, nerve, and the urge to make something with our name on it run hotter. We want to be looked at doing the thing we are proud of, not just to have done it. Confidence comes cleanest when it has something generous to point at: a project, a person, or a cause worth making visible.
exemplars.turn: The catch is that Leo measures by applause, and applause is a fickle ruler. The same heat that makes us bold can make us touchy about credit, quick to put on a show, and slow to stay when somebody else has the spotlight. Build from the inside out and people notice. Chase the clout directly and watch it land on somebody else.
moves: Put one piece of work worth showing where other people can see it.
Give credit out loud before asking for our own.
Choose one project worth the spotlight and finish its visible version.

exemplars.hook: Pressure rises and we tighten up. For about two and a half days, everything gets weighed against the plan. The Moon gets serious here, and so do we.
exemplars.lived: Feelings get translated into tasks: make the list, keep the promise, handle the thing before it becomes a problem. Competence feels comforting, but it can also become armor. We stay busy enough to avoid admitting that something hurts.
exemplars.turn: The catch is treating every feeling like a problem to solve. Not everything difficult is a failure, and not everything tender needs a plan. Do what is ours to do, then leave room to be human off the clock.
moves: Name the feeling before turning it into another task.
Leave one nonessential item unfinished and ask what the pressure was protecting.
Ask for help with one responsibility we keep treating as proof of competence.

exemplars.hook: The conversation we have been avoiding is already obvious. Mercury's move into Cancer changes the voice in the room: thinking and talking turn protective, intuitive, and feeling-led, and words that would not come before may come easier now. Say the thing while the channel is open.
exemplars.lived: For the next few weeks, memory sits in on every conversation. We hear the tone behind the words, remember how the last version went, and decide what feels true before we can explain why. The right sentence can reach somebody here because it sounds like a person, not a press release.
exemplars.turn: The catch is speaking in hints and resenting people for missing them. Sensitivity can make the message kinder, or it can make the message impossible to find. Say what happened, name what is needed, and leave the scavenger hunt out of it.
moves: State what happened before explaining what we think the other person meant.
Ask for the response we need instead of hoping someone reads the tone.
Revisit one family conversation with the missing sentence written down first.

exemplars.hook: What gets called picky is often taste getting clearer. Venus in Virgo turns attraction practical. Want what actually works, not what photographs well.
exemplars.lived: For about four weeks, affection, taste, and money all bend toward the useful: the gesture that actually helps over the grand one, the person who remembers how we take our coffee over the one who stages romance. Venus here reads love as attention, clocking what someone needs before they ask and quietly handling it.
exemplars.turn: Push practical love too far and it curdles: help hardens into control, and care shows up as a list of corrections. We start loving people by fixing them, or earning our keep by staying useful until there is nothing left over. Care lands best with no invoice attached. Try to be needed instead of loved and end up with neither.
moves: Do one useful thing for someone without correcting how they receive it.
Before buying, name the daily problem the purchase will actually solve.
Ask what support would help instead of deciding for the other person.

exemplars.hook: The collective mood drops below the surface. Small things land harder, silence gets louder, and we start reading for what people are not saying.
exemplars.lived: For about two and a half days, feelings get heavier and more private: less said out loud, more felt in the gut. This is the fastest hand on the clock, a passing tone rather than a chapter. It is sharp while it lasts and mostly gone in a few days.
exemplars.turn: The pull is to test the people we love, to poke at a bond to see if it holds, or to go quiet and make them guess. Scorpio feelings want the truth, but they will settle for control when the truth feels too exposed. Say the raw thing and it clears. Hold it in and it leaks out sideways, aimed at whoever is closest.
moves: Ask the direct question instead of testing whether someone notices the silence.
Write down the fact, the fear, and the story built between them.
Give the feeling one honest sentence before it turns into suspicion.

exemplars.hook: The old doubt about being allowed to go first gets loud again. Chiron in Aries presses on the right to want things, take up space, and act without attaching a written apology.
exemplars.lived: Chiron sits in a sign for years, so a whole generation carries this tender spot together. We see it in whose anger is allowed, who gets called selfish, and what happens when somebody finally stops asking permission.
exemplars.turn: The wound shows up two ways: freezing when it is time to assert, or overcorrecting into aggression to cover the freeze. Both are the same bruise, and staying small does not heal the fear of being too much. Taking up room means learning that the discomfort can be survived.
moves: Make the request without adding a reason that makes it easier to refuse.
Take one visible first step before confidence arrives.
When anger rises, name the boundary underneath it before choosing the fight.

exemplars.hook: Some structures do not reform; they compost. Pluto in Aquarius is taking apart the arrangements that stopped serving anyone and growing something stranger in their place.
exemplars.lived: Pluto takes about twenty years to cross a sign, so this is an era, not a mood. In Aquarius it goes to work on power itself: who holds it, who it runs through, and how much of it now lives in networks, machines, and crowds instead of a few hands at the top. The systems we treat as permanent are exactly the ones being quietly rebuilt.
exemplars.turn: The shadow is the group that swallows the person: control dressed up as progress, the crowd deciding it speaks for everyone. Pluto keeps exposing which shared structures serve the many and which only claim to. We do not get to opt out of an era this size. We only get to decide what we are helping to build inside it.
moves: Trace one shared rule back to the person or institution that benefits from it.
Protect the dissenting voice before the group decides it speaks for everyone.
Put time behind one collective project whose power is actually shared.
